extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, students of literature, and educated readers interested in the nature and value of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and standards Shelley uses to define, evaluate, and defend poetry: its functions, moral effects, sources of value, and signs of greatness, as argued in 'A Defence of Poetry.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's highest utility (durable, universal pleasure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasure in its highest sense is durable, universal, and permanent; poetry is useful when it strengthens and purifies the affections, enlarges the imagination, and adds spirit to sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shelley contrasts two senses of utility: the narrow, immediate utility that meets animal wants, and the higher utility that produces lasting moral and imaginative good. Evaluate poetry by its capacity to produce the latter (e.g., 'strengthens and purifies the affections, enlarges the imagination').

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as producer of the highest pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The production and assurance of pleasure in this highest sense is true utility. Those who produce and preserve this pleasure are poets or poetical philosophers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge poetic works by their ability to engender enduring, universal delight and spiritual enlargement rather than merely transient amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's social and political influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry acts as herald, companion, and follower of the awakening of a people and is the most unfailing attendant of beneficial change in opinion or institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a poet/work mobilizes public feeling, reshapes manners or opinions, or contributes to reforms (Shelley cites abolition of slavery and emancipation of women as consequences linked to poetic influences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as creative source of knowledge and power
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is the centre and circumference of knowledge; it comprehends all science and is that to which all science must be referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the generative function of poetry — its capacity to create new materials of knowledge, imagination, and human power which other disciplines then follow or translate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical faculty is two-fold (creation + ordering)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functions of the poetical faculty are two-fold: it creates new materials of knowledge and power and it engenders the desire to reproduce and arrange them according to a rhythm and order called the beautiful and the good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both aspects in a work: originality (new materials or insight) and the artist's ability to organize those materials into aesthetic/moral unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspiration and spontaneity (not subject to will)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is not like reasoning; it is not a power to be exerted at will. A man cannot simply say 'I will compose poetry.' The mind in creation is like a fading coal awakened by an invisible influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value signs of genuine inspiration — freshness, spontaneity, an organic emergence of image and feeling — over merely manufactured or purely mechanical verse. Shelley cites Milton's 'dictated' muse and Milton conceiving Paradise Lost as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic and formal invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets may create language and forms (Dante 'created a language... in itself music and persuasion'); poetic language should have music, persuasion, and the power to create new idioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess innovation in diction, syntax, and the creation or revitalization of literary idiom; musicality and persuasive force are marks of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to make the best moments immortal
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is the record of the best and happiest moments of the happiest and best minds; it arrests vanishing apparitions and sends them forth among mankind, making immortal what is best and most beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a poem's power to capture and transmit fleeting, intense experiences across time and to reanimate such experiences in readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative/alchemic power (transmutation of things)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry turns all things to loveliness; it exalts the beautiful, adds beauty to the deformed, marries exultation and horror, grief and pleasure; its secret alchemy can change forms it touches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge poetry by its ability to transmute ordinary or grotesque subjects into forms of imaginative beauty and to reconcile opposites into a unified effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral elevation and influence on virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry engenders the enthusiasm of virtue, love, patriotism, and friendship; it is linked with the finest impulses and makes men more amiable, generous, and wise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether poetry uplifts ethical sensibility, promotes generous impulses, or refines character rather than merely titillating base desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to reconcile pleasure with pain (tragic sympathy)
rubrics_metrics.description: From an inexplicable defect of harmony in human nature, the pain of the inferior is frequently connected with the pleasures of the superior portions of our being; tragedy delights by affording a shadow of the pleasure which exists in pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a work’s ability to produce complex affective states (e.g., bittersweet pleasure, the pleasure in sorrow) and to use suffering as a means of higher aesthetic or moral insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and inexhaustibility (a great poem as an ever-flowing fountain)
rubrics_metrics.description: A great poem is a fountain for ever overflowing with the waters of wisdom and delight; veil after veil may be undrawn and new relations ever developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure longevity and layered richness: whether repeated readings reveal new meanings, relations, or pleasures across different readers/ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic truth and relation to the age
rubrics_metrics.description: The epic poet is one whose creations bear a defined and intelligible relation to the knowledge, sentiment, and religion of the age and of ages that follow, developing in correspondence with their development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large-scale works, assess whether they systematically reflect and shape the moral, intellectual, and religious consciousness of their era (Shelley names Homer, Dante, Milton as examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's resistance to mere calculation and mechanistic reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: While reasoners and mechanists may be useful in limited functions, if their speculations lack correspondence with first principles of imagination they can exacerbate social ills; poetry provides counterbalance to pure calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value poetry’s attention to the imaginative first principles that humanize scientific or economical knowledge; beware of works that reduce poetry to didactic calculation or marketable formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as sensitive, morally serious temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets tend to be delicately organized, sensitive to pain and pleasure beyond others; their sensibility enables them to experience and communicate the ethereal states that are the material of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating poets' authority or authenticity, consider their depth of feeling and imaginative responsiveness as relevant credentials (Shelley links this to their capacity to reanimate past emotions in others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original conception vs mere imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: True epic or great poetry involves original creation rather than mere imitation; many imitators ('mock-birds') do not fulfill conditions of epic truth or genuine poetic creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between works that genuinely create new imaginative worlds or principles and those that are skillful but derivative imitation; originality of conception is a decisive factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's role in cultural continuity and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry and the poetical principle outlived periods of darkness, blended with other cultures, and contributed to the revival of arts and moral sentiments; no nation or religion supersedes another without incorporating poetic elements of that which it supersedes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a work's participation in cultural transmission, synthesis, or renewal — its capacity to mediate between inherited forms and new cultural needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as source of moral imagination (bridging knowledge to action)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have more moral, political and historical wisdom than we know how to reduce into practice; we 'want the creative faculty to imagine that which we know' — poetry supplies the imaginative force to convert knowledge into action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether poetry catalyzes practical moral imagination — whether it inspires readers beyond cognition to the will to act or to envision better institutions/practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical greatness recognized by posterity despite personal faults
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest poets' errors and personal faults have been weighed and found dust in the balance; fame and the moral authority of great poetry survive the poet's personal failings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for artistic evaluation that separates aesthetic and cultural achievement from private moral failings; prioritize the lasting imaginative effects of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's inseparability from ethical and aesthetic order (poetry as universal order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry has a common source with all other forms of order and beauty; it supplies an organizing principle according to which human life’s materials may be arranged into beauty and good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works for their capacity to impose coherent aesthetic and ethical ordering on chaotic material — coherence, proportion, and the integration of parts into a meaningful whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of inspired composition vs laborious manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: The finest passages of poetry are produced by inspired moments; toil and delay may only mean careful observation of inspired moments and artificial connexion between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging technical polish, weigh the presence of inspired intensity higher than sheer labor-intensive craftsmanship; technical revision should serve inspiration, not replace it.
